detail.longDescription: I'm trying to work with the new Python 3.15/PEP-814 frozendict . The new type has operations to add and update values using the union operator. This always returns a new frozendict , which is expected and good. Example: >>> foo = frozendict(x=1) >>> foo frozendict({'x': 1}) >>> bar = foo | { 'y': 2 } >>> bar frozendict({'x': 1, 'y': 2}) But it doesn't look like there's a way to create a new frozendict with one or more items removed from it. Other languages have similar constructs but also have delete or intersection operations. For example C#'s ImmutableDictionary.Remove or Scala's - on Map. Is there anything similar I can use in frozendict ?
